title: Why ownership changes the building process
description: Clean output and portable content are product decisions, not export features.
text: ownership is easiest to promise at the end and hardest to preserve throughout a product. we think it should shape the editor, data model and publisher from the beginning. output is part of the interface a visitor experiences the page, not the builder. semantic structure, compact styles and predictable loading are therefore part of the authoring experience. portability disciplines the system when content and design can be understood outside the editor, internal convenience is less likely to leak into the public page. that constraint improves both performance and longevity.

title: Public web foundation
description: The independent Fuma public site foundation and safe projection boundary.
text: the fuma public site now has an independent application boundary, kenya-first acquisition journeys and validated public projections. included website and publication journeys validated documentation collections authority-backed pricing and discovery states secure opaque transitions into the application technical seo and privacy controls

title: Getting started with Fuma
description: Choose a publishing profile and prepare your first project.
text: start by deciding what you want to publish. choose **website** for flexible pages and structured business content, or **publication** for a recurring editorial workflow. create your project use the start link from the matching product page. fuma passes only an opaque intent to the application. sign in there, confirm the current choices, and create your project. build the first page add a page, place semantic modules on the canvas, and use the design controls to establish colour, typography and spacing. publish deliberately preview the result before publishing. draft changes remain private until you choose to publish them.

title: Publishing and clean output
description: Understand previews, drafts and immutable public releases.
text: publishing creates visitor-facing output from the content and design state you approve. draft edits do not replace the active release. preview before release use preview to inspect responsive layouts, links and content without changing the public site. static by default pages that do not need per-visitor data are emitted as semantic html and compact css. dynamic behaviour is reserved for features that actually need it. roll forward safely a later publish creates a new release. the active release remains an explicit choice rather than an in-place mutation.

title: Safe components and code examples
description: Use reviewed MDX callouts and code examples without exposing executable markup.
text: the public content compiler accepts only reviewed components declared in strict frontmatter. start with [the publishing guide](/docs/publishing#preview-before-release). reviewed callouts preview content before publication. a callout is rendered as semantic aside content and never executes authored code. escaped code next steps return to [getting started](/docs/getting-started#create-your-project) when you are ready to build.

title: Plan a small business website
description: A practical sequence for a clear, useful business website.
text: begin with the decision a visitor needs to make. a clear business site usually needs fewer pages than its first outline suggests. name the outcome write one sentence describing what a good visitor should understand or do. use it to test every section. build the minimum path explain the service in plain language show credible examples answer common concerns make contact easy check the result review the site at a narrow viewport, zoom the browser, use the keyboard, and read the page without images before publishing.

title: Acceptable use notice
description: Safety rules for Fuma public pages, forms, and any separately activated service.
text: use public fuma surfaces lawfully and without harming people, systems, or rights. product-specific acceptable-use terms may add rules before a service is activated. prohibited activity do not use fuma surfaces to distribute malware; phish; spam; impersonate; harass; exploit or endanger children; violate privacy; infringe rights; evade access, rate, or payment controls; manipulate traffic; or disrupt a service. do not test with another person’s account or data, run destructive or high-volume security activity, upload live secrets or harmful payloads, or keep information reached without authorization. public forms use security reporting for a vulnerability concern and contact for a concise abuse report. include only the public url or identifier and the minimum context needed. form acceptance does not confirm delivery, investigation, outcome, or response time. safety response an owning authority may reject or limit a request that violates these rules or threatens safety. any product restriction, suspension, appeal, evidence retention, or legal action requires the applicable authority and product terms; this public website does not claim those operations have occurred. review state independent legal and trust-and-safety approval for production launch remains pending. this notice makes no certification, monitoring-coverage, enforcement-speed, or regulatory claim.

title: Cookies and browser storage notice
description: Storage used by the Fuma public website and the boundaries around optional measurement.
text: the fuma public website does not issue an application, identity, administration, member, or tenant session cookie. it does not set a parent-domain session cookie. essential operation page delivery and bounded submissions may process request headers, a replay token, form age, and short-lived process-memory anti-abuse keys. the contact route does not set a cookie and returns no-store responses. optional measurement optional measurement remains off until you choose it. if allowed, the public site stores a versioned preference in session storage for this host. the preference is not a product session and is not made available to product or tenant hosts. global privacy control or do not track disables the optional path. blocking optional measurement does not block essential page delivery or the server-side validation of a form request. change your choice use the on-page privacy control to choose essential-only behavior or clear this public host’s session storage. a changed policy version requires a fresh compatible choice rather than silently extending an earlier one. approval state this notice describes repository-backed public-site behavior. production privacy approval and any provider-specific disclosure remain pending; no analytics, advertising, or consent certification is claimed.

title: Public website privacy notice
description: What the Fuma public website collects, why it is used, and which production details remain pending approval.
text: this notice covers the fuma public website. it does not describe a signed customer contract, a production provider arrangement, or every product, member, tenant, payment, or administration workflow. information you choose to send a contact form asks for a name, reply email, message, request type, consent-notice version, and random replay token. security, privacy, abuse, and expert inquiry forms add only their routing category or the public expert identifier. do not send passwords, secret keys, identity documents, payment details, health information, or other sensitive records. the browser sends the form to a same-origin server route. that route size-limits and validates the body, rejects unexpected fields and unsafe control characters, and then attempts a server-to-server handoff. an accepted response means accepted for routing; it does not prove delivery or promise a response. anti-abuse processing the public web process uses a hidden empty field, form age, a replay token, and a short rate window. it hashes the reply address together with limited request-address input and a process-only random salt before keeping a rate key. it keeps accepted replay fingerprints for no more than 24 hours in process memory and does not place the contact body in that replay store. these process-local controls are defence in depth, not a distributed abuse service. measurement and browser storage essential page delivery does not require an application, administration, member, or tenant session cookie. optional public-site measurement remains off until you choose it. the choice is versioned in storage for this public host. global privacy control or do not track suppresses the optional path. retention and production approval the public web boundary has the short process-memory periods described above. any central contact retention, deletion schedule, legal hold, delivery provider, and production owner require separate authority and approval; this notice does not invent them. production launch remains blocked until those details and this notice are reviewed. requests and changes use the privacy request page to ask about access, correction, deletion, or this notice. a separate identity-verification process may be needed. submission does not confirm eligibility, completion, or a deadline. the policy history page records the current version and will identify superseded public versions when any exist.

title: Public website terms of use
description: Terms for using Fuma public pages and forms, separate from any future account or paid-service agreement.
text: these terms apply to browsing and using the public fuma website and its public forms. they are not complete account, subscription, payment, hosting, support, or service terms. a contracting entity and product-specific terms must be presented and approved separately before a paid or hosted service is activated. public information public pages are informational. pricing, availability, entitlements, promotions, templates, experts, plugins, and other mutable facts are valid only when returned by their owning authority at the point of action. an unavailable authority produces an unavailable state rather than an editorial substitute. nothing on this website promises a provider, certification, compliance result, uptime percentage, service level, incident history, contact delivery, support response, feature date, or uninterrupted access. permitted use you may browse public pages and send genuine, bounded requests. do not interfere with operation, bypass controls, misrepresent identity or authority, submit malicious material, probe other people’s data, automate abusive traffic, or use forms for spam. external and product transitions a link or handoff does not itself create an account, contract, purchase, entitlement, or endorsement. the destination must validate current authority and present any applicable terms before action. configured external links use https and do not receive a public-site product session from this website. availability and changes a page or integration may be unavailable, withdrawn, or changed. current policy metadata shows its effective date, version, review role, and review due date. no superseded public version exists yet; future versions must retain the earlier text in policy history. approval state independent legal approval for production launch remains pending. these repository-published website terms do not claim that approval has occurred and should not be treated as professional legal advice.
